**Teens, Social Media and Technology 2024**  
(URL: [https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2024/12/12/teens-social-media-and-technology-2024/](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2024/12/12/teens-social-media-and-technology-2024/))

*(Published Dec 2024\)*

* **Most teens use social media and have a smartphone, and nearly half say they’re online almost constantly**  
* **YouTube tops the list** of online platforms asked about in survey (9 in 10 teens report using the site, slightly down from 95% in 2022\)  
  * **73% of teens say they go on YouTube daily**, making YouTube the most widely used *and* visited platform asked about  
    * Includes share of **15% who describe their use as “almost constant”**  
* **TikTok, Instagram and Snapchat remain widely used among teens** (roughly six-in-ten teens say they use TikTok and Instagram, and 55% say the same for Snapchat)  
  * **About 6 in 10 visit TikTok daily**  
    * Includes **16% who report being on it almost constantly**  
  * **Roughly half of teens say they go on Instagram or Snapchat every day**  
    * Includes about **1 in 10 who say they’re on each of these platforms almost constantly**  
    * Share of teens using Instagram almost constantly has increased slightly, from 8% in 2023 to 12% today   
* **Facebook and X use have steeply declined over the past decade** (today, 32% of teens say they use Facebook, down from 71% in 2014-15, though the share of teens who use the site has remained stable in recent years; 17% of teens say they use X, about half the share who said this a decade ago (33%) and down from 23% in 2022\)  
* **Roughly one-quarter of teens (23%) say they use WhatsApp,** up 6 percentage points since 2022  
  * Relatively few teens report using Facebook daily (20%)   
* **14% of teens use Reddit**, share that has remained stable over past few years  
* **Across all five platforms, one-third of teens use at least one of these sites almost constantly**

![][image2]

* By gender:  
  * Teen girls are more likely than boys to say they use TikTok almost constantly (19% vs. 13%)  
    * Teen boys are more likely than girls to use YouTube this often (while 19% of boys say they use it almost constantly, that share drops to 11% among girls)  
  * Unlike last year, similar shares of boys (13%) and girls (12%) today say they use Snapchat almost constantly  
  * No gender differences in the shares of teens who report using Instagram and Facebook almost constantly  
  * Instagram & TikTok are used more widely by teen girls than teen boys (66% of girls say they use TikTok, compared w/ 59% of boys)  
    * Instagram use follows similar pattern (66% vs. 56%)    
  * Boys more likely than girls to say they use YouTube (93% vs. 87%)   
* By race & ethnicity:  
  * Roughly one-quarter of Black (28%) or Hispanic (25%) teens say they visit TikTok almost constantly   
    * Share drops to 8% among White teens  
  * Black and Hispanic teens are also more likely than White teens to say they constantly use YouTube or Instagram  
  * Few to no racial/ethnic differences in shares visiting Snapchat and Facebook on near constant basis  
  * Among teens, larger share of those who are Black (79%) or Hispanic (74%) than White (54%) say they use TikTok  
    * Black and Hispanic teens also stand out compared w/ White teens in their use of Instagram and X  
  * When it comes to WhatsApp, Hispanic teens are more likely than Black or White teens to say they use it  
* By age:  
  * Older teens are more likely than younger teens to use each of the platforms asked about  
    * Teens ages 15 to 17 more likely than those ages 13 to 14 to say they use Instagram (72% vs. 43%) or Snapchat (63% vs. 44%)  
  * Differences more modest for platforms like YouTube, which most older (92%) and younger (87%) teens use  
* By household income:  
  * Facebook remains more commonly used among teens in lower-income households   
    * 45% of teens in households earning less than $30,000 a year say they use Facebook – drops to 35% among teens in households earning $30,000 to $74,999 a year and 29% among teens w/ household incomes of $75,000 or more  
  * Teens in lower-income households are more likely than those in the highest-income households to say they use TikTok (73% vs. 59%)  
* By partisanship:  
  * Teens who identify as Democrats/Democratic learners more likely than Republicans/GOP learners to say they use TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Reddit, and WhatsApp  
  * TikTok stands out for partisan difference: 73% of Democratic teens vs. 52% of Republican teens report using the platform  
* **Nearly half of teens say they are online almost constantly,** up from 24% a decade ago (share has stayed consistent over past few years)  
* Nearly all teens – 96% overall – report using the internet daily   
  * About half or more Hispanic (58%) or Black (53%) teens say they use internet almost constantly – share drops to 37% among White teens  
  * About half of 15 to 17-year-olds report that they are online almost constantly, compared w/ 38% of those ages 13 to 14
